name: Aiwend – AI Chatbot
author: ERFAN TEYMOURIKALGODARI

sections.description:
Visitors keep asking the same questions, and the answers are often already on your site. Aiwend adds an AI chatbot that answers from the pages, posts and text files you choose, lists the sources it used, and says so when your content does not contain the answer. Bring your own key: connect your own account at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, and the provider bills you, not Aiwend. Aiwend has no server and no subscription, sends nothing to its author, and does not host or resell AI models. Usage limits you set, including a site limit, stop the assistant when they are reached. AI answers can still be wrong, so test before visitors see it. Developed by Erfan Teymouri.

Aiwend also includes tools for drafting content, WooCommerce product text, inquiries and read-only access for an AI app you authorise. All six modules are free and switched off after activation, so you turn on only what you need.

This is a public beta (0.11.0). Each of the seven connections (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter and GroqCloud) was exercised with a real provider account using sample content only; OpenRouter only partly, and not every free model works. Everything else is tested with recorded sample responses. Providers change their services without notice, so expect rough edges, try Aiwend on a staging site first, and set a spending limit at your AI provider as well as in Aiwend. The interface is available in 30 languages: English plus 29 bundled translations. The translations are AI-assisted drafts that no native speaker has reviewed (see the FAQ).

What is included

  • Answer visitor questions from your own content (Chat and Knowledge). Create an assistant with its own name, instructions, look and AI model. Add knowledge from published posts and pages, or from uploaded TXT or Markdown files. The assistant answers only from sources you attach and mark Public, and each answer lists the sources it used. If the sources do not contain the answer, it says so. Show it inline with the “Aiwend Chat” block or the [aiwend_chat bot="ID"] shortcode, or as a floating launcher.
  • Stay in control of cost. A site usage limit (assistants do not answer until you set one), per-conversation and per-visitor daily limits, a pause switch, and an administrator view of conversations with export and delete. Limits count “units” (an estimate of text size), not money; your provider’s invoice can differ.
  • Draft posts and pages (Content Studio). Write a brief, review the proposed draft, edit it, and save it as a WordPress draft. Nothing is published for you.
  • Improve WooCommerce product text (WooCommerce AI, needs WooCommerce). Pick a simple or variable product, choose which fields to send as reference and which fields to replace, and review the proposal. Price, SKU, stock, status and other fields are never changed.
  • Collect inquiries (AI Forms). Add an inquiry form with [aiwend_form id="N"]. Messages stay on your site for administrators. Nothing goes to an AI provider unless an administrator presses Analyze on one message, and Aiwend sends no emails.
  • Connect an AI app, read-only (MCP). An optional endpoint for AI apps that you connect with an application password. It offers nothing until you tick a tool, and it cannot change anything.

How it works with your own API key

You create an API key at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, add it under Aiwend > AI Connections, and press Check access. The key is stored encrypted on your site. Answers and their cost go through your own provider account; Aiwend does not provide free AI usage.

Not available

Meaning-based (embedding) search, human handoff, order or customer assistants, automatic emails, tools that change the site through MCP, and OAuth for MCP are not part of this plugin. Aiwend works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter and GroqCloud only. See the FAQ for what the AI model cannot do.
This edition does not read PDF files; add that content as a post, a page or a text file.

Deactivation and uninstall

  • Deactivating stops scheduled jobs and removes the chat widget and routes; all Aiwend data stays in the database.
  • Deleting the plugin keeps all data by default (tables wp_aiwend_*, options aiwend_*), so reinstalling restores everything.
  • To remove everything on delete, turn on Aiwend > Settings > Privacy > “When the plugin is deleted” > permanently delete (you must type DELETE). It then removes, for that site, the tables, options, capabilities and scheduled job, and the key file when no site on the installation keeps its data (saved provider keys then become unrecoverable). It cannot be undone.
  • Your posts, pages, media and users are never deleted. AI providers keep their own records.

Requirements

Minimums: PHP 8.1 with the json, sodium and mbstring extensions; WordPress 7.0 or newer (tested on 7.0.7 and 7.1.3); InnoDB. Tested with WordPress 7.0.7 and 7.1.3 and WooCommerce 11.2.1 and 10.9.4, on Linux (Apache and nginx) and Windows. Full integration tests ran on PHP 8.1 and 8.3; PHP 8.2 and 8.4 had compatibility checks; unit tests ran on PHP 8.1 to 8.5. PHP 8.5 has not had integration testing.

Database versions: Aiwend supports MySQL 8.0 or newer and MariaDB 10.11 or newer. The suites were run on MySQL 8.0.46 and 8.4.11 and MariaDB 10.11.14 and 11.4.13 (unit tests with real-database variants, the integration suite, and install and uninstall checks); other patch versions of those series are expected to work. Newer series (for example MySQL 9 or MariaDB 11.8) were not individually verified; no problem is known and Aiwend shows no warning for them. Servers older than the minimum are not supported and Aiwend then shows a notice. MySQL 8.0 reached upstream end of life in April 2026: keep it patched through your host or move to 8.4. Aiwend never blocks activation because of the database version.

Other requirements: an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, with billing (or the provider’s own free plan) set up at the provider.

External services

Aiwend contacts an AI provider only after an administrator connects their OWN account, and only for the actions below. Nothing is sent when settings are opened or saved, no provider is contacted by default, and Aiwend never switches to another provider on its own. Aiwend has no server and sends nothing to its author. It loads no scripts, styles, fonts or images from other servers.

  • OpenAI (https://api.openai.com). “Check access” sends your API key to the model list endpoint. A chat answer sends the assistant’s instructions, the visitor’s conversation and the text excerpts of the sources used. “Send test message” sends one fixed test message. API customer terms (Services Agreement): https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ How API data is handled (Data controls in the OpenAI platform): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data OpenAI’s general privacy policy, which covers its websites and consumer services and does not govern API customer content: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/
  • Anthropic (https://api.anthropic.com): the same purposes. Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google Gemini API (https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com): the same purposes (Google AI Studio keys; Vertex AI is not supported). Terms: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • DeepSeek (https://api.deepseek.com): the same purposes. Terms: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html Privacy: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html
  • xAI (https://api.x.ai; the Grok models): the same purposes. Terms for API use (enterprise terms): https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service-enterprise Data processing addendum: https://x.ai/legal/data-processing-addendum Privacy policy: https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy xAI’s general privacy policy does not necessarily cover API content. xAI’s published security FAQ (https://docs.x.ai/developers/faq/security) says it keeps API requests and responses for a limited period by default and offers an optional team-level Zero Data Retention (ZDR) setting that Aiwend cannot see or change. xAI’s Enterprise Terms (version dated October 27, 2026) restrict knowingly submitting Personal Data through the API and expect reasonable efforts to prevent end users doing so, unless ZDR is used, and they incorporate the addendum. If visitors or customers may type personal data into a chat or form, read these documents and check your xAI team’s ZDR status before connecting xAI. Aiwend does not check ZDR and does not stop visitors typing personal data; for assistants that use xAI it adds the sentence “Please do not enter personal information.” to the chat notice and shows a warning on the xAI connection screens. These notices do not make a site compliant. Because of this, visitors cannot chat with an assistant that uses xAI unless the site owner allows it in wp-config.php (see the FAQ). Reasoning models bill their reasoning as output.
  • OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai): the same purposes, but OpenRouter forwards each request to the company that hosts the model you choose, so that company also receives your data. By default Aiwend asks OpenRouter to use only providers that, according to OpenRouter, do not collect user data (provider.data_collection=deny; a site developer can relax this with the aiwend_openrouter_data_collection filter). This does not mean Zero Data Retention: OpenRouter and the serving provider may still process and temporarily handle a request as their own policies describe, and Aiwend does not use OpenRouter’s separate zero-data-retention option. A model with no such provider is refused, which can include free models; free models also have low request limits, and a refused or interrupted request may leave its usage unconfirmed until an administrator resolves it. OpenRouter’s model pages show each provider’s data policy. Aiwend never picks a model for you and adds no fallback; if you choose a routing model (for example openrouter/auto), OpenRouter decides which model answers and Aiwend records the model it reports. Terms: https://openrouter.ai/terms Privacy: https://openrouter.ai/privacy Logging by model providers: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/privacy/provider-logging
  • GroqCloud (https://api.groq.com; not xAI’s Grok): the same purposes. Free plans have rate limits and models are retired on published dates. Terms: https://groq.com/terms-of-use Privacy: https://groq.com/privacy-policy
  • Content Studio and WooCommerce AI send your brief or the selected product fields and the instructions to your connected provider only when someone starts a generation. AI Forms sends one stored message only when an administrator presses Analyze; visitors’ submissions never reach a provider by themselves.
  • MCP makes no outbound request. It lets an application that you authorise with an application password read the data described below from your site; that application and its AI service are not controlled by Aiwend.
  • Your provider may charge your account for these requests and may keep its own records; providers may handle data differently on free and paid plans. Aiwend’s unit budget limits what Aiwend sends; it is not your provider’s invoice, and local deletion cannot erase a provider’s copy.
  • Answers are streamed through the WordPress HTTP API (wp_remote_post). These requests are HTTPS only, verify certificates, do not follow redirects, contact only the hosts above, and obey WP_HTTP_BLOCK_EXTERNAL, WP_ACCESSIBLE_HOSTS, the WordPress proxy constants and the pre_http_request filter. The aiwend_streaming_enabled filter (return false) switches streaming off. Stop: when a visitor presses Stop, Aiwend stops showing and processing the answer, keeps the part already received and closes the connection to the AI provider (through the WordPress http_api_curl action). Whether the provider stops generating or billing is up to the provider, so Aiwend records a stopped answer as “usage unknown” and holds its reservation as uncertain. An administrator resolves such holds on the Usage page, by entering the usage from the provider’s own records or by charging the held amount as an unconfirmed estimate; Aiwend never settles them on its own.
  • Code for an OpenAI embeddings request exists but is switched off and cannot run in this build; meaning-based search sends nothing.

Privacy

  • Consent and visitor notice. Nothing leaves your site until an administrator connects their own provider account and turns on a module. The chat shows visitors a short notice under the message box that answers can be wrong and that messages and selected source excerpts are sent to the configured AI provider. As the site owner you decide whether that is enough for your visitors and your local law, and you should mention the provider in your own privacy policy.
  • What is stored. Chat messages and sessions are kept in your database and deleted after 30 days by default (Aiwend > Settings > Privacy). Audit events record actions and outcomes, not message content (30 days by default). Usage records (request IDs and unit counts, no message content) are kept for spending control. Knowledge text and its index are kept until you delete the source; uploaded files are stored as text in the database, not in the uploads folder.
  • Cookie. A visitor’s chat uses a random cookie (aiwend_chat_, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, up to 24 hours); only a hash of it is stored.
  • Abuse limits. Aiwend uses a keyed hash of the visitor’s network address (an IPv6 address as its /64 network), never the address itself, for message and conversation limits (kept for minutes) and for the daily limit (a hash that changes every day, kept for about two days). Signed-in visitors are counted by account number. Administrators see only counts.
  • Providers. When an assistant answers, the data described under “External services” leaves your site. The store:false setting on OpenAI requests disables response storage but does not promise zero retention. Closing the stream does not prove that remote processing or billing stopped. If you use a page-caching plugin, clear its cache after changing an assistant’s AI connection so visitors see the current provider disclosure.
  • AI Forms. A submission stores the optional name, email address, topic and message, a creation and expiry time and, if analysed, the administrator’s AI result. Submissions are deleted after 30 days by default (1 to 365 days) and an administrator can delete any message at once. No IP address, user agent or user ID is stored.
  • MCP. Requests are logged as tool name and outcome only, never arguments, results or credentials. Tools return the site name and language, a list of published pages or posts, and the text of one published, public, non-password-protected page or post; text you do not want an AI service to read should not be published.
  • Aiwend adds text to the WordPress privacy policy guide and supports the WordPress personal data export and erasure tools (conversations of signed-in users, AI Forms by email address). Guests can delete their own conversation in the chat. These controls alone do not make a site compliant with any privacy law.

Source code

All PHP, JavaScript and CSS in this plugin is shipped as written: nothing is minified, compiled or generated, and there is no build step for it. The only bundled library, symfony/polyfill-mbstring, is installed with Composer from composer.json (composer install –no-dev) and its unmodified source is in the vendor folder.

License

Aiwend’s own code and the Aiwend symbol images (assets/brand/aiwend-symbol-64.png, -128.png, -256.png) are licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version (SPDX: GPL-3.0-or-later); the full text is in the LICENSE file. Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices, listed in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (symfony/polyfill-mbstring is MIT).

Third-party notices

See THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Aiwend (Plugins > Add Plugin, shown as Add New in some WordPress versions, or Upload Plugin). All modules are off after activation.
  2. Open Aiwend > Overview and follow its checklist; it shows what is still missing.
  3. In Aiwend > Settings > Modules turn on Chat and Knowledge. Create an assistant, add knowledge (a page, post or text file), mark it Public and attach it to the assistant.
  4. Nothing to set up for the encryption key: Aiwend derives it from the secret keys and salts in your wp-config.php. If those are missing or still the sample text, the AI Connections screen says so and tells you to add an AIWEND_SECRET_KEY line to wp-config.php (see OPERATIONS.txt in the plugin folder). Aiwend creates no key file.
  5. Add a connection (a name and the API key from your provider: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud) and press Check access. It asks the provider for its model list (no text is generated); after it succeeds, choose a model.
  6. Set a site usage limit, test the assistant privately, then add it to a page.
  7. On low-traffic sites add a server cron job so background jobs (indexing, clean-up) run on time.

Back up the database and the encryption key together. Without the key, saved provider keys cannot be decrypted after a restore and must be entered again. Backups, key moves, proxies, limits and other advanced topics are in OPERATIONS.txt, in the plugin folder (wp-content/plugins/aiwend).
sections.faq:
Is Aiwend free?

Yes. All six modules are included at no charge, with no paid tier and no licence key. You pay your AI provider directly for the requests your site makes, so set a spending limit there as well as in Aiwend.

Do I need an AI account?

Yes. You need an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, with billing (or the provider’s own free plan, where it offers one) set up at the provider. Aiwend does not include AI usage. A ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini app subscription is a different product and does not provide an API key. Aiwend cannot tell you in advance what it will cost: your provider charges per request, prices differ by provider and model, and Aiwend’s usage limits count “units”, not money.

Will the chatbot make things up?

It can still be wrong. The assistant is instructed to answer only from the sources you attached and marked Public, it lists the sources it used, and it says so when they do not contain the answer. An AI model can still misread or misstate a source, and Knowledge search matches words rather than meaning, so a question phrased very differently from your text may find nothing or the wrong passage. Test the questions your visitors are likely to ask before you publish the assistant, and review conversations under Aiwend > Conversations.

What happens to my visitors’ messages?

Chat messages are stored in your database (30 days by default) and, to produce an answer, sent to the AI provider you connected together with the assistant’s instructions and the text excerpts of the sources used. The chat shows visitors a short notice about this. See “External services” and “Privacy” below, and mention your provider in your own privacy policy.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes, for product text only. WooCommerce AI proposes a title and descriptions for simple or variable products (for a variable product, only its own title and descriptions) and replaces only the fields you tick. It does not answer questions about orders or customers, and it never changes price, stock, SKU or status.

Can I use it as an FAQ or knowledge base chatbot?

Yes. Add your FAQ pages, posts or text files as knowledge, mark them Public and attach them to the assistant. Search matches words rather than meaning, so keep the content visitors need in the language they ask in.

How do the limits work?

Aiwend counts text in “units” (an estimate of tokens, about one unit per three characters). Units are not money and your provider’s invoice can differ. Before each answer Aiwend reserves an upper estimate against every limit at once; if any limit is reached, nothing is sent to the provider. There is a site limit (you set it), a per-conversation limit, a per-visitor daily limit, a pause switch and message-rate limits. They protect against one heavy visitor, not against many visitors together: the site limit and a spending limit at your provider are your real protection, and Aiwend cannot guarantee that no charge happens at your provider. Defaults and developer filters are in OPERATIONS.txt.

Which languages does the interface support?

Thirty interface languages in total: English, plus 29 bundled translations that need no extra download: Arabic, Bengali, Chinese (simplified and traditional), Czech, Dutch, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Persian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Urdu and Vietnamese. They are AI-assisted drafts: no native speaker has reviewed them and WordPress.org has not approved them, so some wording may be unnatural. By default the interface follows the language chosen in WordPress. Each user can instead pick their own language for Aiwend’s screens with the “Aiwend language” control at the top of every Aiwend screen; this affects only that user and only Aiwend, never the site, other users or other plugins. The chat widget uses the site’s language, and the assistant’s answers follow the language of your content and of the visitor’s question. The fixed message shown when your content has no answer appears in the site’s language when a translation exists. Regional variants that are not listed, such as Austrian German or Mexican Spanish, show English unless WordPress.org provides a language pack for them. Corrections are welcome in the support forum.

What is MCP, and is it safe to turn on?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets an AI app that you authorise read data from a service. Aiwend’s MCP endpoint is optional, off by default, read-only, and offers nothing until you tick a tool. It needs an application password and refuses browser sessions. See “How do I use MCP safely?” below.

The assistant does not answer.

Open Aiwend > Overview: the checklist and “System readiness” show what is missing (Chat and Knowledge turned on, an active public assistant, an AI connection whose access check passed, knowledge attached, and a site usage limit). Usage-limit messages mean one of the limits on the Usage page was reached.

Which AI provider should I choose?

Aiwend does not choose for you and has no preferred provider. Prices, free plans, request limits, model quality and data handling differ by provider and change over time; each provider’s terms are linked under “External services” below. A cautious way to start: use a provider whose billing you already manage, choose a lower-cost model, set a spending limit at the provider as well as the Aiwend site usage limit, and test on a staging site. Each of the seven connections was exercised with a real provider account using sample content only (OpenRouter only partly). Visitor chat on an assistant that uses xAI is off by default; see the xAI question below.

How is Aiwend different from a hosted chatbot service?

Aiwend runs inside your WordPress site and has no server of its own. Your content, conversations and settings are stored in your own database, you choose the provider and the model, and the spending limits are enforced by your site. The text needed to produce an answer (the visitor’s message, the assistant’s instructions and the relevant excerpts of your sources) is sent to the AI provider you connected; see “External services” and “Privacy” below. The trade-off: you manage your own provider account, and Aiwend does not offer features that need a central service, such as human handoff.

What does “Check access” prove, and what do the models cost?

Check access only confirms that the key can list models; it does not prove that a particular model answers well or that a provider’s free plan will serve your requests. Prices differ by provider and model and change over time; Aiwend does not bundle prices for DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, so cost reports show “price unknown” for them instead of a guess.

What can the AI model not do here?

The AI model cannot call tools or functions, read images or audio, generate images or return a fixed data format on request: Aiwend sends text and shows text. Finding sources is by matching words, not meaning, so a question phrased very differently from the source text may not find it.

Can visitors chat with an assistant that uses xAI?

Not by default. xAI keeps API requests for a limited period unless Zero Data Retention (ZDR) is set up on your xAI team, and xAI’s terms for API use may restrict sending personal data without it. Visitors type free text, and Aiwend cannot see or check your ZDR setting. So Aiwend refuses visitor messages to an assistant that uses xAI, hides its chat window from visitors, and does not send anything to xAI for them. Private previews, administrator tools, Content Studio and WooCommerce AI still work, and your xAI connection and key are kept. A site owner who has read the xAI terms that apply to their account and has a lawful basis can allow it by adding define( 'AIWEND_XAI_ALLOW_PUBLIC_CHAT', true ); to wp-config.php (on a multisite network, a list of site IDs such as array( 2 ) allows only those sites). This is the owner’s own decision, not a check: Aiwend does not verify ZDR and cannot stop visitors typing personal data. In AI Forms, pressing Analyze on a visitor’s message with an xAI connection needs an extra tick box for the same reason.

How does this version handle limits, uncertain usage and indexing?

A per-conversation budget limits how much one conversation can use. When Aiwend cannot tell what a request cost (for example after Stop), the amount stays held as uncertain on the Usage page until an administrator resolves it from the provider’s records. If WP-Cron is late, Knowledge has a Process now button that runs a few waiting indexing jobs. Knowledge search matches words, not meaning. There is no database schema change from 0.9.0.

“Check access” fails.

The provider could not be reached or rejected the key. Check the key and the provider’s billing, that your server can make outgoing HTTPS requests, and that WP_HTTP_BLOCK_EXTERNAL or a firewall is not blocking the provider host (list it in WP_ACCESSIBLE_HOSTS). No answer is sent to a connection that has not passed the check.

Anthropic says my key is not tied to a workspace.

Anthropic keys can be tied to a workspace or not, depending on how they were created, and Anthropic may refuse a key that is not when no workspace is named. Aiwend does not send a workspace header. If Check access reports this, create a new key inside a workspace in the Claude Console (choose the workspace when you create the key) and use that key.

Who can change what?

Administrators manage everything. Editors can manage the knowledge library by default, but new knowledge starts private and only administrators can approve a source for answers (the aiwend_publish_knowledge capability). Other roles have no access.

Why does the assistant say it cannot find the answer in another language?

Finding the right passage is done by matching words, not by translating, so a question in a language other than your source text has no words in common with it and the assistant says it could not find that information. Nothing is sent to the provider in that case. Keep the content visitors need in the language they ask in.

Why are some of my page’s contents missing from answers?

Aiwend reads the content WordPress stores for the post, with shortcodes removed. Text that a theme, dynamic block or page builder produces only when the page is displayed is not included. Use Knowledge > Inspect text to see what was indexed, or upload the text as a TXT or Markdown file.

Where is the provider key stored?

Encrypted in your database. The encryption key is not in the database: it is AIWEND_SECRET_KEY in wp-config.php or, when that is not set, a key derived from the secret keys and salts in wp-config.php. Aiwend writes no key file. It protects saved provider keys if only a copy of the database leaks; it does not protect them from anyone who can read your site files.

How do I use MCP safely?

Turn MCP on under Aiwend > Settings > Modules, tick only the tools you need under Aiwend > MCP, use HTTPS, and create a separate application password for each app so you can revoke it. Browser sessions are refused, and the user needs the aiwend_use_mcp capability (administrators have it by default). The MCP endpoint was tested with the official TypeScript MCP SDK client; compatibility with other AI apps has not been verified, and apps that need OAuth, streaming or older protocol revisions cannot connect. More in OPERATIONS.txt.

Does AI Forms email me when someone writes?

No. Messages wait in Aiwend > AI Forms. There is no email, webhook or automatic AI reply.

Can I upload PDF files?

Not in this edition. PDF parsing is the riskiest step of a knowledge base, so it is not part of the WordPress.org package; a PDF upload is refused with an explanation, and TXT, Markdown, posts and pages work as usual.

Does Aiwend include logo images?

Yes, one: the Aiwend symbol (three small PNG sizes in assets/brand), shown beside the name in Aiwend’s own admin screens and as the admin menu icon. It is artwork created with an AI image tool for this project, and the developer licenses it, like the rest of the plugin, under the GPL-3.0-or-later. The name and logo are not a registered trademark, and no exclusive rights in the design are claimed. The public chat never shows it: the avatar defaults to the first letter of the assistant’s display name, or an image you choose.

Where do I get help?

Please use the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org. Never post an API key or the contents of wp-config.php in a public forum.

Who develops Aiwend?

Aiwend is developed by Erfan Teymouri, an individual developer. It is not a product of OpenAI, Anthropic or Google, which are independent companies; their names are used only to say which services you can connect.

Aiwend is free to use. If it helps your website, you can optionally support its ongoing development and maintenance through the link at the bottom of Aiwend > Overview. Contributions do not unlock features or provide priority support, and the plugin itself never contacts the donation page; it is only a link you can choose to open.
sections.changelog:
0.11.0

  • New: optional wording aliases for each assistant (Knowledge tab, one rule per line, for example “fabric samples = swatches”). They help the assistant find your own pages when visitors use different words. Aliases add no knowledge and do not make an answer correct: answers still come only from your sources and are cited. Assistants without aliases behave as before. Aliases are stored on your own site and matched there: no extra service and no extra AI provider request is involved.
  • Improved: knowledge search now requires a real shared content word before a page is offered as evidence, so fewer unrelated pages are used. Questions in Arabic or Persian that find nothing are tried once more with common spelling variants (such as Arabic and Persian yeh and kaf, diacritics and digits).
  • Improved: an alias adds almost no search time (the question and the alias wording share one pass over your sources).
  • Database: schema 16 adds one empty column (bots.aliases) automatically on the first load after the update. Nothing else is changed; older versions ignore the column. No change to spending limits or to what is sent to AI providers.
  • Known limits: search still matches words, not meaning, and is not semantic. A one-word alias applies to every question that contains the word. Paraphrases, long pages without headings and Chinese, Japanese or Korean text match less well. The 21 new admin strings appear in English until they are translated.

0.10.3

  • Changed: the plugin can now run in WordPress Playground demos. This is opt-in and works only inside Playground; on every other server the native sodium extension is still required. No database schema change; no change for existing sites.

0.10.2

  • New: an optional per-user “Aiwend language” for Aiwend’s own screens (Automatic follows WordPress, as before). It changes nothing for other users, the site or other plugins, and never changes the chat shown to visitors.
  • Fixed: the chat’s fixed “I couldn’t find that information in the selected sources.” and “earlier answer no longer available” messages were always English; they now follow the site language when a translation exists. Stored conversations are unchanged and older ones show the translated text too. Sources, limits and what is sent to providers are unchanged.
  • Changed: five new interface strings in the 29 bundled translations (AI-assisted drafts). No database schema change.

0.10.1

  • New: the interface is bundled in 29 languages besides English (ar, bn_BD, cs_CZ, de_DE, el, es_ES, fa_IR, fr_FR, he_IL, hi_IN, hu_HU, id_ID, it_IT, ja, ko_KR, ms_MY, nl_NL, pl_PL, pt_BR, ro_RO, ru_RU, sv_SE, th, tr_TR, uk, ur, vi, zh_CN, zh_TW). They are AI-assisted drafts that no native speaker has reviewed and WordPress.org has not approved; a WordPress.org language pack for a locale, if one exists, is used first.
  • Fixed in the translations: the Test conversation label was missing in every language; one formal register in German (Sie), Spanish (usted), Italian (Lei) and Dutch (u); full-width punctuation in Chinese; a restriction in Hungarian that read as a habit.
  • Changed: the plugin loads its bundled translations and the block editor strings from its own languages folder, after any WordPress.org language pack. No database schema change.

0.10.0

  • Public beta. Minimum PHP is now 8.1 (tested: full integration on 8.1 and 8.3, compatibility checks on 8.2 and 8.4, unit tests on 8.1 to 8.5). No database schema change from 0.9.0 (schema 15; older installs are migrated automatically); settings, encrypted connections, assistants, knowledge sources and usage records are kept.
  • Listing: the plugin is now named “Aiwend – AI Chatbot”, with a clearer description, tag set, FAQ order and refreshed screenshots. No change to what the plugin does.
  • New: AI Forms analysis states and reply tone; MCP paging and chunked reading of long posts; faster shared connection reads; WooCommerce 10.9.4 tested alongside 11.2.1.
  • Fixed: right-to-left navigation tabs; page-header landmark structure; long badges wrap on narrow screens.
  • Interface language: English only in this release. Translations are not shipped.

0.9.0

  • New: connections for DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter and GroqCloud (bring your own key). They had only limited checks with sample content, OpenRouter only partly, and a given model or free plan may not work; costs for them are shown as “price unknown”.
  • New: xAI safeguard. Visitor chat on an assistant that uses xAI is refused on the server unless the site owner allows it with AIWEND_XAI_ALLOW_PUBLIC_CHAT in wp-config.php. Aiwend does not check xAI Zero Data Retention. Existing xAI keys and connections are kept; private previews and administrator tools are unchanged. AI Forms Analyze with xAI needs an extra confirmation.
  • New: a per-conversation budget; clearer reports of uncertain (held) usage and a manual way to resolve it; a Process now button for waiting knowledge indexing; more detail in Diagnostics.
  • Unchanged: knowledge search matches words, not meaning; the AI model cannot call tools, read images or audio, or return a fixed data format; no database schema change.

0.8.1

  • Directory presentation only: clearer description, FAQ, tags and screenshot captions in the readme, and the version number. No change to the plugin’s code, database schema, providers or behaviour.

0.8.0

  • Beta release. Chat and Knowledge modules, plus Content Studio, WooCommerce AI, AI Forms and a read-only MCP endpoint (all off by default; new database table for AI Forms, added automatically on update); provider connections for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google Gemini (checked once with real accounts and sample content, otherwise tested with recorded responses); a stopped answer is labelled “Stopped by you” and keeps the text already shown; encrypted provider keys with an optional key file and re-encryption; site, conversation and per-visitor daily usage limits with administrator notices; opt-in permanent deletion on uninstall; word-matching knowledge search with cited sources; GPL-3.0-or-later license.

short_description: AI chatbot that answers from your own content, with sources and usage limits. Bring your own key. Also drafts, WooCommerce text, forms, MCP. Beta.
description:
Visitors keep asking the same questions, and the answers are often already on your site. Aiwend adds an AI chatbot that answers from the pages, posts and text files you choose, lists the sources it used, and says so when your content does not contain the answer. Bring your own key: connect your own account at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, and the provider bills you, not Aiwend. Aiwend has no server and no subscription, sends nothing to its author, and does not host or resell AI models. Usage limits you set, including a site limit, stop the assistant when they are reached. AI answers can still be wrong, so test before visitors see it. Developed by Erfan Teymouri.

Aiwend also includes tools for drafting content, WooCommerce product text, inquiries and read-only access for an AI app you authorise. All six modules are free and switched off after activation, so you turn on only what you need.

This is a public beta (0.11.0). Each of the seven connections (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter and GroqCloud) was exercised with a real provider account using sample content only; OpenRouter only partly, and not every free model works. Everything else is tested with recorded sample responses. Providers change their services without notice, so expect rough edges, try Aiwend on a staging site first, and set a spending limit at your AI provider as well as in Aiwend. The interface is available in 30 languages: English plus 29 bundled translations. The translations are AI-assisted drafts that no native speaker has reviewed (see the FAQ).

What is included

  • Answer visitor questions from your own content (Chat and Knowledge). Create an assistant with its own name, instructions, look and AI model. Add knowledge from published posts and pages, or from uploaded TXT or Markdown files. The assistant answers only from sources you attach and mark Public, and each answer lists the sources it used. If the sources do not contain the answer, it says so. Show it inline with the “Aiwend Chat” block or the [aiwend_chat bot="ID"] shortcode, or as a floating launcher.
  • Stay in control of cost. A site usage limit (assistants do not answer until you set one), per-conversation and per-visitor daily limits, a pause switch, and an administrator view of conversations with export and delete. Limits count “units” (an estimate of text size), not money; your provider’s invoice can differ.
  • Draft posts and pages (Content Studio). Write a brief, review the proposed draft, edit it, and save it as a WordPress draft. Nothing is published for you.
  • Improve WooCommerce product text (WooCommerce AI, needs WooCommerce). Pick a simple or variable product, choose which fields to send as reference and which fields to replace, and review the proposal. Price, SKU, stock, status and other fields are never changed.
  • Collect inquiries (AI Forms). Add an inquiry form with [aiwend_form id="N"]. Messages stay on your site for administrators. Nothing goes to an AI provider unless an administrator presses Analyze on one message, and Aiwend sends no emails.
  • Connect an AI app, read-only (MCP). An optional endpoint for AI apps that you connect with an application password. It offers nothing until you tick a tool, and it cannot change anything.

How it works with your own API key

You create an API key at OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, add it under Aiwend > AI Connections, and press Check access. The key is stored encrypted on your site. Answers and their cost go through your own provider account; Aiwend does not provide free AI usage.

Not available

Meaning-based (embedding) search, human handoff, order or customer assistants, automatic emails, tools that change the site through MCP, and OAuth for MCP are not part of this plugin. Aiwend works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter and GroqCloud only. See the FAQ for what the AI model cannot do.
This edition does not read PDF files; add that content as a post, a page or a text file.

Deactivation and uninstall

  • Deactivating stops scheduled jobs and removes the chat widget and routes; all Aiwend data stays in the database.
  • Deleting the plugin keeps all data by default (tables wp_aiwend_*, options aiwend_*), so reinstalling restores everything.
  • To remove everything on delete, turn on Aiwend > Settings > Privacy > “When the plugin is deleted” > permanently delete (you must type DELETE). It then removes, for that site, the tables, options, capabilities and scheduled job, and the key file when no site on the installation keeps its data (saved provider keys then become unrecoverable). It cannot be undone.
  • Your posts, pages, media and users are never deleted. AI providers keep their own records.

Requirements

Minimums: PHP 8.1 with the json, sodium and mbstring extensions; WordPress 7.0 or newer (tested on 7.0.7 and 7.1.3); InnoDB. Tested with WordPress 7.0.7 and 7.1.3 and WooCommerce 11.2.1 and 10.9.4, on Linux (Apache and nginx) and Windows. Full integration tests ran on PHP 8.1 and 8.3; PHP 8.2 and 8.4 had compatibility checks; unit tests ran on PHP 8.1 to 8.5. PHP 8.5 has not had integration testing.

Database versions: Aiwend supports MySQL 8.0 or newer and MariaDB 10.11 or newer. The suites were run on MySQL 8.0.46 and 8.4.11 and MariaDB 10.11.14 and 11.4.13 (unit tests with real-database variants, the integration suite, and install and uninstall checks); other patch versions of those series are expected to work. Newer series (for example MySQL 9 or MariaDB 11.8) were not individually verified; no problem is known and Aiwend shows no warning for them. Servers older than the minimum are not supported and Aiwend then shows a notice. MySQL 8.0 reached upstream end of life in April 2026: keep it patched through your host or move to 8.4. Aiwend never blocks activation because of the database version.

Other requirements: an API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter or GroqCloud, with billing (or the provider’s own free plan) set up at the provider.

External services

Aiwend contacts an AI provider only after an administrator connects their OWN account, and only for the actions below. Nothing is sent when settings are opened or saved, no provider is contacted by default, and Aiwend never switches to another provider on its own. Aiwend has no server and sends nothing to its author. It loads no scripts, styles, fonts or images from other servers.

  • OpenAI (https://api.openai.com). “Check access” sends your API key to the model list endpoint. A chat answer sends the assistant’s instructions, the visitor’s conversation and the text excerpts of the sources used. “Send test message” sends one fixed test message. API customer terms (Services Agreement): https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ How API data is handled (Data controls in the OpenAI platform): https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data OpenAI’s general privacy policy, which covers its websites and consumer services and does not govern API customer content: https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/
  • Anthropic (https://api.anthropic.com): the same purposes. Terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms Privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google Gemini API (https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com): the same purposes (Google AI Studio keys; Vertex AI is not supported). Terms: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • DeepSeek (https://api.deepseek.com): the same purposes. Terms: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html Privacy: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html
  • xAI (https://api.x.ai; the Grok models): the same purposes. Terms for API use (enterprise terms): https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service-enterprise Data processing addendum: https://x.ai/legal/data-processing-addendum Privacy policy: https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy xAI’s general privacy policy does not necessarily cover API content. xAI’s published security FAQ (https://docs.x.ai/developers/faq/security) says it keeps API requests and responses for a limited period by default and offers an optional team-level Zero Data Retention (ZDR) setting that Aiwend cannot see or change. xAI’s Enterprise Terms (version dated October 27, 2026) restrict knowingly submitting Personal Data through the API and expect reasonable efforts to prevent end users doing so, unless ZDR is used, and they incorporate the addendum. If visitors or customers may type personal data into a chat or form, read these documents and check your xAI team’s ZDR status before connecting xAI. Aiwend does not check ZDR and does not stop visitors typing personal data; for assistants that use xAI it adds the sentence “Please do not enter personal information.” to the chat notice and shows a warning on the xAI connection screens. These notices do not make a site compliant. Because of this, visitors cannot chat with an assistant that uses xAI unless the site owner allows it in wp-config.php (see the FAQ). Reasoning models bill their reasoning as output.
  • OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai): the same purposes, but OpenRouter forwards each request to the company that hosts the model you choose, so that company also receives your data. By default Aiwend asks OpenRouter to use only providers that, according to OpenRouter, do not collect user data (provider.data_collection=deny; a site developer can relax this with the aiwend_openrouter_data_collection filter). This does not mean Zero Data Retention: OpenRouter and the serving provider may still process and temporarily handle a request as their own policies describe, and Aiwend does not use OpenRouter’s separate zero-data-retention option. A model with no such provider is refused, which can include free models; free models also have low request limits, and a refused or interrupted request may leave its usage unconfirmed until an administrator resolves it. OpenRouter’s model pages show each provider’s data policy. Aiwend never picks a model for you and adds no fallback; if you choose a routing model (for example openrouter/auto), OpenRouter decides which model answers and Aiwend records the model it reports. Terms: https://openrouter.ai/terms Privacy: https://openrouter.ai/privacy Logging by model providers: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/privacy/provider-logging
  • GroqCloud (https://api.groq.com; not xAI’s Grok): the same purposes. Free plans have rate limits and models are retired on published dates. Terms: https://groq.com/terms-of-use Privacy: https://groq.com/privacy-policy
  • Content Studio and WooCommerce AI send your brief or the selected product fields and the instructions to your connected provider only when someone starts a generation. AI Forms sends one stored message only when an administrator presses Analyze; visitors’ submissions never reach a provider by themselves.
  • MCP makes no outbound request. It lets an application that you authorise with an application password read the data described below from your site; that application and its AI service are not controlled by Aiwend.
  • Your provider may charge your account for these requests and may keep its own records; providers may handle data differently on free and paid plans. Aiwend’s unit budget limits what Aiwend sends; it is not your provider’s invoice, and local deletion cannot erase a provider’s copy.
  • Answers are streamed through the WordPress HTTP API (wp_remote_post). These requests are HTTPS only, verify certificates, do not follow redirects, contact only the hosts above, and obey WP_HTTP_BLOCK_EXTERNAL, WP_ACCESSIBLE_HOSTS, the WordPress proxy constants and the pre_http_request filter. The aiwend_streaming_enabled filter (return false) switches streaming off. Stop: when a visitor presses Stop, Aiwend stops showing and processing the answer, keeps the part already received and closes the connection to the AI provider (through the WordPress http_api_curl action). Whether the provider stops generating or billing is up to the provider, so Aiwend records a stopped answer as “usage unknown” and holds its reservation as uncertain. An administrator resolves such holds on the Usage page, by entering the usage from the provider’s own records or by charging the held amount as an unconfirmed estimate; Aiwend never settles them on its own.
  • Code for an OpenAI embeddings request exists but is switched off and cannot run in this build; meaning-based search sends nothing.

Privacy

  • Consent and visitor notice. Nothing leaves your site until an administrator connects their own provider account and turns on a module. The chat shows visitors a short notice under the message box that answers can be wrong and that messages and selected source excerpts are sent to the configured AI provider. As the site owner you decide whether that is enough for your visitors and your local law, and you should mention the provider in your own privacy policy.
  • What is stored. Chat messages and sessions are kept in your database and deleted after 30 days by default (Aiwend > Settings > Privacy). Audit events record actions and outcomes, not message content (30 days by default). Usage records (request IDs and unit counts, no message content) are kept for spending control. Knowledge text and its index are kept until you delete the source; uploaded files are stored as text in the database, not in the uploads folder.
  • Cookie. A visitor’s chat uses a random cookie (aiwend_chat_, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, up to 24 hours); only a hash of it is stored.
  • Abuse limits. Aiwend uses a keyed hash of the visitor’s network address (an IPv6 address as its /64 network), never the address itself, for message and conversation limits (kept for minutes) and for the daily limit (a hash that changes every day, kept for about two days). Signed-in visitors are counted by account number. Administrators see only counts.
  • Providers. When an assistant answers, the data described under “External services” leaves your site. The store:false setting on OpenAI requests disables response storage but does not promise zero retention. Closing the stream does not prove that remote processing or billing stopped. If you use a page-caching plugin, clear its cache after changing an assistant’s AI connection so visitors see the current provider disclosure.
  • AI Forms. A submission stores the optional name, email address, topic and message, a creation and expiry time and, if analysed, the administrator’s AI result. Submissions are deleted after 30 days by default (1 to 365 days) and an administrator can delete any message at once. No IP address, user agent or user ID is stored.
  • MCP. Requests are logged as tool name and outcome only, never arguments, results or credentials. Tools return the site name and language, a list of published pages or posts, and the text of one published, public, non-password-protected page or post; text you do not want an AI service to read should not be published.
  • Aiwend adds text to the WordPress privacy policy guide and supports the WordPress personal data export and erasure tools (conversations of signed-in users, AI Forms by email address). Guests can delete their own conversation in the chat. These controls alone do not make a site compliant with any privacy law.

Source code

All PHP, JavaScript and CSS in this plugin is shipped as written: nothing is minified, compiled or generated, and there is no build step for it. The only bundled library, symfony/polyfill-mbstring, is installed with Composer from composer.json (composer install –no-dev) and its unmodified source is in the vendor folder.

License

Aiwend’s own code and the Aiwend symbol images (assets/brand/aiwend-symbol-64.png, -128.png, -256.png) are licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version (SPDX: GPL-3.0-or-later); the full text is in the LICENSE file. Third-party components keep their own licenses and notices, listed in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (symfony/polyfill-mbstring is MIT).

Third-party notices

See THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

screenshots.caption: Front-end chat: answers are taken from your own pages and each answer lists its source. Shown in the built-in simulated demo, which contacts no AI provider and is labelled on screen.
Knowledge library: add pages, posts or text files, and see which are ready and used in answers. Search matches words, not meaning, and the screen says so.
Assistant editor: write the instructions and try the real chat widget privately before visitors see it.
Overview: see at a glance what is set up and what is still missing, including your site usage limit.
Content Studio input form (before generating): describe the post or page you want, then review the result before saving a draft. Nothing is published for you. Form only; no generated text is shown.
WooCommerce AI input form (before generating): choose a simple or variable product and what is sent as reference. Prices, stock and SKU are never changed. Form only; no generated text is shown.
AI Forms inbox: messages stay on your site; nothing is emailed or sent to an AI provider unless you press Analyze.

Retrieval abstention: when your sources do not contain the answer, the assistant says so instead of guessing. Shown in the built-in simulated demo, which contacts no AI provider and is labelled on screen.

Usage and limits: see what has been used, reserved and is still available, and set a site limit and a per-conversation limit. Units are Aiwend's own count, not money, and a usage limit is not a spending cap, so also set a spending limit with your AI provider. Figures are from a demo site.

Wording aliases: optional rules for one assistant that map your visitors' words to the words your pages use. They help word matching only and add no knowledge. Two example rules are typed in the editor box and not saved.
